Synod of Ulster
sin'-ud uv ul'-ster
n. (the Synod of Ulster, 1690–1840, the governing assembly of the Presbyterian ministers of the north of Ireland)
Greek sunodos, a coming together, a way travelled in company; Ulster, the northern province of Ireland.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

The Synod of Ulster was the governing assembly of the Presbyterian ministers planted in the north of Ireland by the Scots settlement of the early seventeenth century. Its seed was the presbytery erected at Carrickfergus in 1642 by the chaplains of the Scottish army, the first presbytery in Ireland; by 1659 there were five presbyteries, and after the Revolution of 1688 they met as one body, which from 1690 sat annually and governed the northern church for a hundred and fifty years. It was no establishment and never held the civil sword. Its ministers were sustained by their own people and by the royal bounty, and its courts had only the authority of the word, which is the only authority a church court ever truly has. The synod ordained and examined, visited congregations, planted new ones, disciplined the scandalous, and sent its deputies to the General Assembly in Scotland. The pattern was apostolic and deliberately so: “And the apostles and elders came together for to consider of this matter” (Act 15:6). Its annals are the annals of Irish Presbyterianism — the Pacific Act of 1720, the subscription quarrel that cost it the Presbytery of Antrim in 1726, the long Arian decay of the eighteenth century, and the orthodox recovery under Henry Cooke which ended in the union of 1840 and the General Assembly of the Presbyterian Church in Ireland.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines a synod as an ecclesiastical council, and a presbytery as a body of elders in the Christian church.

expand to see more

SYN'OD, n. A council or meeting of ecclesiastics to consult on matters of religion.

PRES'BYTERY, n. A body of elders in the Christian church.

ORDA'IN, v.t. To set apart for an office; to invest with ministerial functions.

Key Scripture

Act 15:6 — "And the apostles and elders came together for to consider of this matter."

1Ti 4:14 — "Neglect not the gift that is in thee, which was given thee by prophecy, with the laying on of the hands of the presbytery."

Tit 1:5 — "For this cause left I thee in Crete, that thou shouldest set in order the things that are wanting, and ordain elders in every city, as I had appointed thee:"

Act 20:28 — "Take heed therefore unto yourselves, and to all the flock, over the which the Holy Ghost hath made you overseers, to feed the church of God, which he hath purchased with his own blood."

Modern Corruption

The assembly of the Ulster Scots, apostolic in pattern and unestablished in standing.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The synod is worth knowing because it answers a charge still made against presbyterian order — that courts of review are a human invention bolted onto a congregational New Testament. The Ulster ministers had no bishop, no parliament and no endowment to lean on; they met because Scripture shows apostles and elders meeting, and they held that a minister is ordained by a presbytery and not by a congregation acting alone.

The principle to recover is the one Paul left with Titus, that a church is not finished until it is ordered: “that thou shouldest set in order the things that are wanting, and ordain elders in every city” (Tit 1:5). A synod that forgot this became, within three generations, a court that could not say what its own ministers believed.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Greek sunodos (G4923), a company travelling together; presbuterion (G4244), a body of elders; episkopos (G1985), an overseer.

expand to see more

Greek sunodos (G4923) — a company journeying together; Luke 2:44.

Greek presbuterion (G4244) — the body of elders, the presbytery; 1 Timothy 4:14.

Greek presbuteros (G4245) — an elder; Acts 15:6.

Greek episkopos (G1985) — an overseer, bishop; Acts 20:28.

Greek kathistemi (G2525) — to appoint, ordain; Titus 1:5.

Usage

"“the apostles and elders came together” (Act 15:6) — the warrant for a synod."

"“the laying on of the hands of the presbytery” (1Ti 4:14) — how Ulster ordained."

"“ordain elders in every city” (Tit 1:5) — the work of a hundred and fifty years."
